small_guidance:
- Add a GROUP_M block-swizzle (e.g. 8) to gemm_bias_kernel for better L2 reuse across N tiles, since M=128, N=16384, K=16384 — the N dimension dominates and L2 thrash on A reads is the bottleneck.
- Expand autotune to include larger BLOCK_K (64, 128) with num_stages=4 to better overlap K-loop loads for K=16384; also try BLOCK_M=32 configs since M=128 only yields 4 row tiles at BLOCK_M=32 vs 1-2 currently.
- Increase softmax BLOCK_SIZE to 4096 or 8192 with num_warps=16, and consider a single-pass online softmax (running max + correction factor) to halve global memory traffic on the 128×16384 tensor.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a split-K / streamK GEMM since K=16384 is huge and M=128 is small — current grid only launches ~128 programs total (M/64 × N/128 = 2×128 = 256), severely underutilizing the 4090's 128 SMs when each program has a long serial K loop. A split-K with atomic accumulation or a 2-stage reduction would expose far more parallelism.
- Fuse softmax directly into the GEMM epilogue: since each row of the output (16384 elements) is produced by all N-tiles of one M-row, use a persistent kernel per row that accumulates the full row in SRAM/registers, then does online softmax in the same kernel — eliminates the 128×16384 fp32 write+read between GEMM and softmax (~8MB of HBM traffic).
- Alternatively, keep GEMM and softmax separate but use an online (single-pass) softmax with running-max correction, cutting softmax HBM reads from 3× to 1× the tensor.
